references.text: The Lord says He will go down to see Sodom and Gomorrah, in a similar way as He went down to see the city and tower at Babel.
The Lord says 'Let us go down' – a direct continuation of the action in verse 5, where God intervenes in human plans.
The Lord says He has come down to deliver Israel, using the same Hebrew expression (ירד) as in Genesis 11:5.
The Lord looks down from heaven and sees all mankind, reflecting God's sovereign observation of humanity at the Tower of Babel.
David speaks of it being impossible to flee from God's presence, reflecting God's omniscience and ability to observe human actions.
Both verses illustrate God's active investigation of humanity, either to judge pride (Babel) or to seek righteousness (Psalm 14).
Both verses describe the Lord's 'descent' as a prerequisite for judgment against human rebellion or sin.
Micah 1:3 confirms the theological pattern in Genesis 11:5: the Lord's descent always marks an act of judgment against human rebellion.
